title: Affine centred section charts and their Rees comparison maps
statement: Let S be Noetherian and g:V->S smooth separated finite type of pure relative dimension d with a closed section s and s;g=id [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion]. An affine centred chart consists of an affine open b:T->S, an affine open j:U->V times_S T, a closed section r:T->U with r;j the base-changed s, and a separated etale map e:U->A^d_T over T whose square with r, id_T and zero is Cartesian [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-sbc-affine-space], [def-pc-fibre-product]. Using the actual section-ideal extended-Rees construction [def-pur-dnc-section-family], define reesBase, reesOpen and reesCoordinates by the coefficient maps t->t, b/t->image(b)/t, the last followed by the standard identification x_j=t*u_j. Package only the geometric properties of these fixed maps needed for locality, and supply their well-definedness: finite-type Noetherian domains, separated etale chart maps, compactifiable structural maps, the Cartesian base square and the augmentation/structural equations. When g and q are compactifiable, define localSourceMap and localFamilyMap by the actual section base-change mate [def-pur-noetherian-section-specialization-arrows], then open-chart locality and the affine chart map [def-trf-section-local-comparison-data]. Adjunctions of the specified affine right functors are parameters of the construction. No isomorphism of dualizing fibres is supplied as chart data.
